name: Maine
headline_status: Recreational and medical cannabis are legal for adults 21+ in Maine.
summary: Maine voters narrowly legalized adult-use cannabis in 2016, and licensed stores opened October 9, 2020; the medical program dates to a 1999 ballot vote. On January 1, 2026 the retail sales tax on adult-use cannabis rose to 14% while the per-pound cultivation excise tax fell by a third. A citizen initiative to repeal adult-use sales and home growing missed the 2026 ballot deadline but has until June 2027 to qualify for the November 2027 ballot.

adult_use_since.value: Approved by voters in November 2016 (Question 1, 50.26%); licensed retail sales began October 9, 2020.

possession_limit.value: Adults 21+ may possess up to 2.5 ounces of cannabis, or 2.5 ounces of cannabis and concentrate combined, of which no more than 10 grams may be concentrate.

home_grow.value: Adults may grow up to 3 mature plants at home, or on another adult's property with written permission. Medical patients may also grow.

retail_sales.value: Licensed adult-use stores have operated since October 9, 2020 (first licenses issued September 8, 2020). All products must pass contaminant testing and are tracked statewide.

taxes.value: Since January 1, 2026: 14% sales tax on adult-use cannabis, plus a cultivation excise tax of $223 per pound of flower and $63 per pound of trim (cut from $335 and $94).

medical_program.value: Maine has no fixed list of qualifying conditions; a clinician may certify a patient for any condition. Patients may grow their own, use a caregiver, or buy from medical dispensaries or adult-use stores.

regulator.value: Office of Cannabis Policy (OCP), within the Department of Administrative and Financial Services, created in February 2019.

public_use.value: Adults may consume only in a private residence or on private property not open to the public with the owner's permission. Using cannabis as a driver or passenger in a vehicle on a public way, or smoking in public, is a civil violation with a fine of up to $100.

dui.value: Impairment-based: Maine has no THC per se or zero-tolerance law, so a cannabis OUI requires evidence of impairment.

tourists.value: Yes. Adults 21+, residents or not, may buy up to 2.5 ounces of adult-use cannabis (including no more than 10 grams of concentrate) from licensed stores.

timeline.event: Question 1 legalizes adult-use cannabis by a 3,995-vote margin after a recount
Adult-use sales tax rises to 14% and cultivation excise tax is cut by one-third (LD 210)
Repeal initiative misses the signature deadline for the 2026 ballot

pending.item: A SAM Action-backed citizen initiative would end licensed adult-use sales and ban home growing for adults, effective January 1, 2028.
pending.status: Collecting signatures; needs 67,682 valid signatures by June 8, 2027 for the November 2027 ballot

faq.a: Yes. Adults 21 and older can possess up to 2.5 ounces and buy from licensed stores, and Maine also runs a medical program.

faq.q: How many plants can you grow in Maine?
faq.a: Adults may grow up to 3 mature plants at home, or on another adult's property with written permission.

faq.q: What is the cannabis tax in Maine?
faq.a: Since January 1, 2026, adult-use purchases carry a 14% sales tax, and growers also pay a per-pound excise tax.
Not yet. A repeal initiative missed the 2026 ballot and is trying to qualify for November 2027.
